theme: Opting out of isolation: nonisolated unsafe, default isolation and upcoming features

terms.definition: A keyword that tells the compiler to skip isolation checks for a variable you protect yourself.
terms.example: Mark the global nonisolated unsafe only if you guard it.
terms.code:
nonisolated(unsafe) var level = 1
func bump() { level += 1 }
bump()
print(level)

terms.definition: A build setting that puts code on the main actor unless you say otherwise.
terms.example: New app targets use the main actor as the default isolation.
terms.code:
import PackageDescription
let package = Package(name: "Kit", targets: [
    .target(name: "Kit", swiftSettings: [
        .defaultIsolation(MainActor.self)
    ])])

terms.definition: A compiler flag that turns on a future Swift behavior early, one feature at a time.
terms.example: Enable the upcoming feature in the package settings.
terms.code:
import PackageDescription
let package = Package(name: "Kit", targets: [
    .target(name: "Kit", swiftSettings: [
        .enableUpcomingFeature(
            "NonisolatedNonsendingByDefault"
        )])])

Today's terms

Default Isolation - A build setting that puts code on the main actor unless you say otherwise.
Upcoming Feature - A compiler flag that turns on a future Swift behavior early, one feature at a time.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Nonisolated Unsafe, Default Isolation and Upcoming Feature in English?

dialogue.title: The new project settings

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I made a new target in Xcode 26, and my code runs on the main actor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the default isolation. New targets can use the main actor as the default.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I do not write `@MainActor` on every type?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. You only opt out when something should run elsewhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I also see a list of upcoming feature flags in the settings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An upcoming feature turns on a future Swift behavior early, one flag at a time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. But my global `level` still shows an error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is anything protecting it? You can mark it nonisolated unsafe if you guard it yourself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I guard it with a lock, so that is safe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then nonisolated unsafe is fine. Without a guard, it hides a real data race.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Default isolation and an upcoming feature for the target.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And nonisolated unsafe only for guarded globals.
Mark the global nonisolated unsafe only if you guard it.
